capabilities: Switch each device between Standard, Lite and Extreme start modes that control which community plugins load
Tick plugins for the Lite start list and load or unload plugins for the current session
Show window memory and running plugin count in the status bar with a popup for mode switching
Restart Obsidian directly in a chosen start mode via commands
Move itself to the top of the community plugin list so start-up interception works
disambiguation: Not a runtime memory cleaner; it saves memory by skipping plugins at start-up, since unloading them mid-session frees little.
extras: Desktop only and requires Obsidian 1.13.0+. Relies on non-public Obsidian internals (app.plugins, community-plugins.json order), so an Obsidian update could change behaviour; a fail-safe loads plugins normally if the plugin is removed or disabled. Renamed from Plugin Memory Monitor (id plugin-monitor) in 0.4.0. Ko-fi donations accepted.
motivation: Older laptops, low-RAM PCs and shared or virtual desktops feel the cost of every Obsidian plugin, and the author found unloading plugins mid-session frees almost nothing.
problem: Loaded community plugins keep most of their memory until restart, so on low-RAM machines the only reliable saving is to not load unneeded plugins at start-up, which Obsidian cannot do per device.

relations.evidence: With BRAT: add mohammedsuder/obsidian-memory-saver as a beta plugin.

summary: Start-up mode manager that loads only the community plugins a device needs and shows Obsidian's memory use and plugin count in the status bar.
